doc.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Concierto rhythm section; Chet Baker; the snowstorm
summary: Roland Hanna, Gadd, and Chet's remark, then a snowed-in session.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Yeah, that’s Allan Ganley. That’s my British friend, that one. That’s…
There was a helluva rhythm section on that, too.
Yeah, Roland was beautiful. And Ron and…
Yeah, Steve Gadd, yeah. I had never, I didn’t know anything about Steve Gadd at all. That was kinda… it worked out okay, too, with Steve, too.
And one of the tunes on there is Mom’s, isn’t it?
Oh, yeah, yeah. That was cute. The Answer Is Yes. Was it that one?

I didn’t know Chet Baker well. I knew about him for years and everything, and he had a really rough life. And he was really a hippy from… (laughs) So we’re looking at this tune. The Answer Is Yes. And Chet sees Jane Herbert Hall and so he says… He looks at me and says, “A chick wrote that, man? Wow.” (laughs) I still remember that. That’s the only thing he said to me the whole time. “A chick wrote that, man. Wow.” And then, another… I don’t know if it was that CD or what, but I was doing some editing… it might have been up at Rudy Van Gelder’s and it was a huge snowstorm. So I’m there. It was just Rudy and Creed Taylor and me. Not a terribly compatible, fun group. And it was a huge snowstorm. And I said, “Oh no, I’m gonna have to be…” And fortunately, and George Price, our friend the cartoonist, lived nearby. So somehow I got plowed out of there and I called George and I went and stayed overnight at George’s, George’s house but… But it was a great recording studio, though, so…
